creator: Claude Code (claude-sonnet-5-5) worker session tien-nghich-2d-26 (lane B, mist_archive), 2026-11-22; operator tien-nghich-2d-26
method: create_character_pro_flash (32x32 native, low top-down, dog template, 8 views, 40-colour palette, seed 7) then animate_character v3 per direction (keep_first_frame=false, palette passed; canvases come back 36-44 px and are centred on 32 by the build script). All four facings are separate PixelLab generations; nothing is mirrored. Diagonal direction_prompts keys are required by the tool and were filled with 'unused diagonal: ...' placeholders; no diagonal was generated.
prompt: Small folio hound, a stocky dog-like beast standing on all four legs, its body made of stacked parchment folios bound with a bronze-studded leather spine strap, cream-white page-edge ruffs on the chest and tail, dark ink-grey muzzle and legs, a long tail of loose pages, bright vermilion seal stamp on the forehead, large ears like folded pages. 3/4 top-down, chunky pixel art, 1px dark outline, light from top-left.

idle.action_description: stands on all four legs breathing gently, the page-leaf tail and ears twitch slightly, the red seal stays on the forehead

direction_prompts.south: facing the viewer on all four legs, breathes gently, ears and page tail twitch slightly
direction_prompts.west: facing left on all four legs, breathes gently, page tail sways behind on the right
direction_prompts.north: seen from behind on all four legs, breathes gently, page tail sways
direction_prompts.east: facing right on all four legs, breathes gently, page tail sways behind on the left

idle.regeneration_action_description: stands on all four legs breathing gently, only the body and the page tail move slightly, no marks, no sparks, no breath clouds, the red seal stays on the forehead

regeneration_direction_prompts.west: facing left on all four legs, breathes gently, only the body and page tail move slightly; nothing appears in front of the muzzle, no marks, no sparks

walk.action_description: trots forward on all four legs in a quick walk cycle, page tail streams behind, red seal stays on the forehead

direction_prompts.south: trots toward the viewer on all four legs in a compact narrow trot, only the legs move, tail stays directly behind
direction_prompts.west: trots to the left on all four legs, page tail streams out to the right behind it
direction_prompts.north: trots away from the viewer, seen from behind, on all four legs, tail swaying
direction_prompts.east: trots to the right on all four legs, page tail streams out to the left behind it

telegraph.action_description: crouches low on all four legs and rears its head back, page ruffs bristle and spread, preparing to lunge, no effects

direction_prompts.south: facing the viewer, crouches low, head draws back, page ruffs bristle, stays compact
direction_prompts.west: facing left, crouches low, head draws back, page ruffs bristle, tail stays behind on the right
direction_prompts.north: seen from behind, crouches low, page tail and ruffs bristle
direction_prompts.east: facing right, crouches low, head draws back, page ruffs bristle, tail stays behind on the left

strike.action_description: lunges forward and snaps its jaws, body stretches forward then springs back, page tail flicks, no effects

direction_prompts.south: facing the viewer, lunges toward the viewer and snaps its jaws, then springs back, stays compact
direction_prompts.west: facing left, lunges forward to the left and snaps its jaws, then springs back, tail behind on the right
direction_prompts.north: seen from behind, lunges forward away from the viewer, then springs back
direction_prompts.east: facing right, lunges forward to the right and snaps its jaws, then springs back, tail behind on the left

frame_count_note: The mob profile wants 3 frames for idle and telegraph but PixelLab v3 only returns even counts (min 4). Idle was generated with 4 frames and the last was dropped; telegraph with 4 and frame 1 was dropped (kept 0, 2, 3, renumbered 0-2). The raw folder holds the kept frames only; the dropped ones were never shipped.
